sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Abolition of Zamindari Policing**: In **1791**, Lord Cornwallis stripped Indian **Zamindars** of their traditional police functions and land-revenue-cum-police levies to curb local tyranny and consolidate Company control.
• **Introduction of the Daroga System**: Districts were divided into police jurisdictions (thanas) of roughly **20 square miles**, each placed under an Indian officer known as a **Daroga**, appointed by and directly accountable to the British Magistrate.
• **Separation of Revenue and Police**: Aligned with the **Cornwallis Code**, police functions were completely detached from revenue collection, concentrating magisterial and police oversight in the hands of the **District Magistrate**.
• **Urban Policing Extension**: The system was extended to major cities like Calcutta, Dhaka, and Murshidabad, introducing urban watch and ward mechanisms.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Maintained by Zamindars, local paiks, and watchmen (chowkidars). Rural Bengal.
Decentralized, corrupt, inefficient, and prone to extortion and private armies.
Illustrates pre-colonial and early Company reliance on indigenous intermediaries.
District thanas headed by Darogas. Supervised by English Magistrates. Bengal Presidency.
Centralized bureaucratic control, fixed jurisdiction, paid through state funds (initially via fees/fines).
Primary target of UPSC Prelims chronology and administrative reform questions.
All-India uniform police structure under Police Act of 1861 following the 1860 Police Commission.
Paramilitary character, provincial commissioner/IG control, suppression of dissent.
Contrasts sharply with the 1791 district-magistrate-daroga model.

items.definition: An Indian police officer in charge of a local police station (thana) introduced in 1791, later notorious for corruption and oppression due to inadequate salaries and unchecked localized power.
A defined police jurisdiction or station area covering approximately 20 square miles, established to systematize crime reporting and law enforcement.
The focal British official who exercised direct supervision over the Darogas, merging executive magisterial control with police administration.
Legislative package that formalized the administrative, judicial, and police reforms initiated in 1791, laying the foundation of the British administrative state in India.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Bengal Presidency**: The primary testing ground for the 1791 police reforms, extending outward to Bihar and Orissa.
• **Urban Centers**: Calcutta, Murshidabad, and Dhaka saw tailored adaptations of the thana system to manage denser populations and trade routes.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Darogas became corrupt and oppressive ('Daroga Raj'), exploiting their distance from European magistrates and low official pay.
• **Policy Interventions**: Subsequent reviews led by Bentinck (abolishing the office of Superintendent of Police in divisions) and culminating in the **Police Commission of 1860**.

items.title: Mnemonic for Cornwallis Reforms
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'C-P-D: Cornwallis Pulled Down Zamindari police for Darogas'
• **Decoded Meaning**: Cornwallis (Governor-General), Pulled Down (Abolished Zamindari police), Darogas (Introduced 1791 Daroga system).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly prevents confusion between Warren Hastings' early experiments and Cornwallis's 1791 structural overhaul.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: 1791 = Daroga appointed; 1793 = Cornwallis Code codified it legally alongside the Permanent Settlement.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently confuses the Police Act of 1861 with the 1791 Cornwallis police reforms. Remember that 1791 introduced the *Daroga system and district thanas under Cornwallis*, whereas the 1861 Act created the modern provincial police forces after the Revolt of 1857.

Mains Value Addition: When writing on police reforms or criminal justice administration in GS Papers (History or Internal Security), trace the historical genesis: note how Cornwallis's 1791 model prioritized colonial order and revenue security over civil liberties, setting a legacy of executive control over policing that persists today.

keyTakeaways: Lord Cornwallis abolished the feudal Zamindari police system in 1791 to establish direct state control over law and order.
The 1791 system introduced the Daroga-headed thana model, separating police administration from revenue collection.
Despite aiming to curb corruption, the Daroga system suffered from severe localized extortion ('Daroga Raj'), necessitating further systemic overhauls in the 19th century.
